title: GCC recovery tracker shows initial rebound has stalled
gist: Oxford Economics' GCC recovery tracker shows the rebound stalling: the diffusion index fell 5.4 points to 51.0 in September, with a 5.7% GDP contraction forecast this year and 5.5% growth in 2027. Saudi oil output is at 77% of pre-conflict levels yet its oil and gas revenues exceed them, while Oman outperforms and Kuwait and Qatar lag.

themes.theme: GCC growth path and recovery momentum

insights.claim: Oxford Economics forecasts the GCC economy will contract 5.7% this year before recovering with 5.5% growth in 2027, so the 2027 rebound only partly offsets the current-year hit.
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane
insights.so_what: Regional output stays below its pre-conflict path through 2027, which caps earnings and credit upside for GCC domestic-facing names.
insights.quote: a forecasted GDP contraction of 5.7% for this year, followed by a gradual recovery to 5.5% growth in 2027

insights.claim: The GCC recovery tracker's diffusion index fell 5.4 points to 51.0 in September, barely above the 50 expansion threshold, indicating the initial post-disruption rebound has stalled and recovery is fragile.
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane
insights.so_what: A reading near 50 means breadth of improvement is nearly gone, so upside surprises are less likely near term.
insights.quote: the diffusion index, which fell by 5.4 points to 51.0 in September

themes.theme: Confidence and activity drags in Saudi Arabia

insights.claim: Flight disruptions and falling equity prices drove the GCC slowdown, with ongoing attacks on civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia undermining confidence.
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane
insights.so_what: Security-driven confidence shocks hit aviation, tourism and listed equities first, so these are the channels to monitor for deterioration or relief.
insights.quote: ongoing attacks on civilian infrastructure have undermined confidence
insights.locator: Flight disruptions and declining equity prices

insights.claim: Tourist arrivals have dropped across the GCC and fiscal impacts are uneven, pressuring tourism-dependent diversification sectors even as hydrocarbon income holds up.
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane
insights.so_what: Non-oil diversification stories are more exposed than oil revenue in this shock.
insights.locator: Despite a drop in tourist arrivals

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia has restarted exports and shipping activity shows resilience, yet Saudi oil production is only at 77% of pre-conflict levels, so volumes remain well short of full normalisation.
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane
insights.so_what: Further production recovery toward 100% is a visible upside lever for Saudi output and for oil supply balances.
insights.quote: oil production remains at only 77% of pre-conflict levels

insights.claim: Saudi oil and gas revenues have exceeded pre-conflict levels despite lower production and tourism, demonstrating fiscal resilience, which implies price or mix effects are offsetting volume losses.
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane
insights.so_what: Saudi fiscal stress is less acute than activity data suggests, reducing sovereign funding risk.
insights.quote: Saudi Arabia’s oil and gas revenues have exceeded pre-conflict levels
insights.locator: Despite a drop in tourist arrivals

insights.claim: Oman is performing relatively well thanks to stable energy production, while Kuwait and Qatar continue to lag, so GCC recovery is highly uneven by country.
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane
insights.so_what: Country selection matters more than a broad GCC allocation; Oman is relatively favored, Kuwait and Qatar are laggards.
insights.quote: Oman performing relatively well due to stable energy production, while Kuwait and Qatar continue to lag behind
insights.locator: The outlook varies across the region
